node.name: Push Party by Nia Akilah Robinson
node.descriptionText:
About the show: Nia Akilah Robinson’s Push Party is a lively ensemble comedy about six Black women trying to uphold fifteen years of friendship at a post-birthing party in Harlem. All Lelo wants is for this event to go smoothly, but tensions among the group rise and then explode when an unhoused person lands in the community room. Inspired by Black women’s stories of birth and motherhood and by the joys and challenges of life in Harlem, this new play confronts the moments when friendship erodes, when hope starts to falter, when we argue until we laugh, and when Black folk see other Black folk suffering and die a little inside.

Performance Dates and Times:
Thursday, November 5 @ 8pm 
Friday, November 6 @ 8pm 
Friday, November 6 @ 11pm 
Saturday, November 7 @ 4pm
Saturday, November 7 @ 8pm

node.name: University Church in Yale Worship
node.descriptionText:
The University Church in Yale is a student-focused church welcoming Christian students of all backgrounds, as well as staff, faculty, post-docs, parents, alumnus/a, parents, and our New Haven neighbors.

Our church life is centered around Sunday worship in Yale’s historic Battell Chapel, which features beautiful music, thoughtful preaching, and the prayer of a diverse, faithful community. Outside of Sunday mornings, we have lots of fun together with retreats, study groups, meals, concerts, lectures and other events.

UCY is an open and affirming congregation; we welcome persons of any denominational background (or none), race, ethnicity, age, nationality, sexual orientation, gender identity/expression, or physical or mental ability. Whether you are a life-long Christian, a questioning Christian, or new to Christianity, we hope that you feel at home with us.

node.name: EveryBody Dances with Keerati Jinakunwiphat
node.customTimeInstruction: All levels. 15 and under accompanied by adult
node.descriptionText:
November 08, 2026 | 11am–12:30pm | Dance Studio

Instructions

The Dance Studio is located on the lower level of Yale Schwarzman Center, 168 Grove Street, New Haven, CT 06511.

Free and open to the public with registration.

We welcome people ages 15 and under when accompanied by an adult.
If you need technical assistance with registration or require accessible accommodations contact ysc.info@yale.edu.

Doors open at 10:30am.

EveryBody Dances @ Yale Schwarzman Center brings local and visiting dance artists to our Dance Studio to teach masterclasses in jazz, hip hop, salsa, modern, contemporary, precision dance and more! All community members are welcome. This week's class will be led by Keerati Jinakunwiphat 

Title: Class and Choreography

With the intention of preparing, organizing, and freeing our bodies, Keerati's class begins with connecting to our awareness and sense of self. The class uses the floor to discover tactility, circularity, and shifts of weight to warm up. With this sense of groundedness, the class shifts to exploring different planes and axes to find new ways to move across the room. Going into choreography, musicality and individuality are emphasized as we play with the phrase work. Keerati's class focuses on how we can stay present as we take up and share the space with each other.

node.name: Wisemania Film Series: TITICUT FOLLIES
node.descriptionText:
TITICUT FOLLIES (Frederick Wiseman, 1967, 16mm, 84 mins)
Banned from public exhibition for nearly a quarter century, Wiseman's first documentary is one of his most famous, and arguably his most consequential. Filmed in a state hospital for the criminally insane, it exposes practices that cross the line from care into cruelty, raising questions about dignity, authority, and society’s treatment of the most vulnerable. “An extraordinarily candid picture of a modern Bedlam, where the horrors are composed of indifference and patronizing concern” (Vincent Canby). Few films have looked so directly at institutional power, or demanded so much from their audience. 16mm print from the Yale Film Archive.

“Wisemania” is a multi-year exploration of the works of documentarian Frederick Wiseman.

node.name: Sunday Trivia Nights at Bobbi’s
node.descriptionText:
Trivia at Bobbi’s runs about 90 minutes and is played over five rounds. The game features a slideshow format with image-based and puzzle categories, making it engaging, easy to follow, and accessible for players with hearing difficulties.

Questions span history, science, music, film, television, geography, and more, creating a well-rounded game that appeals to players of all experience levels and interests.

A strong emphasis is placed on teamwork, with categories designed to encourage group thinking and collaboration. Bobbi’s puzzle rounds are especially popular, known for their creativity and memorable “A-ha!” moments.

Trivia at Bobbi’s is always free to play, with prizes and bragging rights for the top-scoring teams. All are welcome!

node.name: Which Habit Type Are You? Unlocking ways to practice regularly
node.foodDetails: Tea & Mochi Social Hour follows at 8pm!
node.descriptionText:
Are you an Upholder, Obliger, Questioner, or Rebel? 

Understanding your tendency can help you find strategies that work for you—in meditation and beyond. Using Gretchen Rubin’s The Four Tendencies, we’ll explore how we respond to expectations, recognize our patterns, and discover ways to make meditation a regular part of our lives.

Beginners, newcomers, and all are welcome, anytime. Taught by Sumi Kim, Buddhist Chaplain.

node.name: Fireside with Davis and Asialene Smith
node.descriptionText:
What does it mean to build a purpose-driven life across business, global service, and faith? Join the LDSSA as we hear from Davis and Asialene Smith for our November fireside.

Davis Smith is a Senior Fellow at Yale’s Jackson School of Global Affairs and the founder of several impact-driven companies, including the social enterprise outdoor brand Cotopaxi. The Smiths recently returned to the U.S. after serving as mission leaders in Brazil. Together, they’ll share insights on entrepreneurship, global service, leadership, and living a gospel-centered life in high-impact spaces.
